chunks: "Both are just silicon with a tiny amount of impurity added on purpose, and the difference is which carrier you have more of.
For N-type I add something like phosphorus, which has five valence electrons.
Four of them bond into the crystal and the fifth is left over and loosely held, so it becomes a free electron.
Electrons are the majority carrier, which is why it's called N for negative carriers. For P-type I add boron, which has three valence electrons.
It's one short of a full bond, so it picks up an electron from a neighbouring atom and leaves a hole.
That hole acts like a mobile positive charge, so holes are the majority carrier. Neither material is actually charged.
The extra electron is balanced by the positive phosphorus ion it left behind, and the same for boron.
And the minority carrier is never zero: in N-type with 10 to the 16 donors per cm³, electrons are about 10 to the 16 , and holes are about 10 to the 4 from np equals n i squared .
Put a P region next to an N region and you get a PN junction, which is where the diode and everything else comes from."
